meta.name: Numerical Reasoning Practice Test 1
meta.subtitle: mathcentre · 23 questions
meta.description: Published by mathcentre with the University of Hertfordshire; questions are based on AssessmentDay and Graduates First.
meta.instructions:
Many employers use psychometric testing in their recruitment process, with numerical reasoning tests often included.

The questions used in the following test are based on those available on the www.assessmentday.co.uk and www.graduatesfirst.com websites.

This test comprises 23 questions and you have 25 minutes to complete it.

The main numerical skills required for the test typically relate to percentages, ratios and reading/interpreting charts and graphs. Often the same data is used for several questions, so it is advisable get a clear grasp of the context before starting your calculations.

Calculators are allowed, so make sure that you are familiar with yours and are confident in using it.

sections.title: Fitness Centre Members
passages: The chart below shows the number of new members by type (i.e. level of membership) at a Fitness Centre each month.

questions.prompt: In which month is the greatest number of new members obtained?
questions.explanation:
The number of new members needs to be added for each month:
February: 20 + 20 + 17 + 15 + 12 = 84
March: 22 + 19 + 17 + 14 + 11 = 83
April: 19 + 18 + 16 + 15 + 14 = 82
May: 21 + 18 + 17 + 15 + 11 = 82
June: 20 + 18 + 16 + 14 + 13 = 81
February has the greatest number (84) of new members obtained.

The answer is A (84).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: In April what percentage (to the nearest whole number) of the new members are Super?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on expressing one quantity as a percentage of another on page 2.
The number of Super new members is 18.
The total number of new members in April is 82.
The percentage of new members in April that registered at Super is: 18 ÷ 82 × 100 = 21.95121̇%, this rounded to the nearest whole number is 22%.

The answer is E (22%).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Over the 5 month period, what is the average number of Deluxe new members per month?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on how to calculate the average of numbers on page 2.
Over 5 months there were 12 + 11 + 15 + 11 + 16 = 65 new members.
The average number of Deluxe new members over the 5 month period is: 65 ÷ 5 = 13.

The answer is C (13).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: In May, what is the ratio of Super new members to Off Peak new members?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition of ratio on page 2.
The number of Super new members in May is 21.
The number of Off Peak new members in May is 15.
The ratio of Super new members to Off Peak new members is 21: 15 which can be simplified to 7: 5 by dividing both numbers by 3.

The answer is E (7: 5).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: What is the best approximation to the percentage increase in Standard new members between February and March?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage increase on page 2.
The number of Standard new members in February is 20.
The number of Standard new members in March is 22.
There is a (22−20) ÷ 20 × 100 = 10% percentage increase in Standard new members between February and March.

The answer is C (10%).

sections.title: Share Portfolio
passages: A client has a portfolio of shares in 5 companies and is reviewing their annual performance.

headers: Number of shares held at 1st Jan

questions.prompt: Which company’s shares contribute the greatest value to the portfolio on 1st January?
questions.explanation:
The contribution value is calculated by multiplying the number of shares by the price per share.
This is done for each company taking the price per share at 1st Jan:
Media: 8,000 × 250𝑝 = £20,000
Insurance: 6,500 × 350𝑝 = £22,750
Retail: 9,000 × 440𝑝 = £39,600
Energy: 13,500 × 300𝑝 = £40,500
Leisure: 20,000 × 190𝑝 = £38,000

The shares of Energy contribute the greatest values to the portfolio on the 1st January.

The answer is D (Energy).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Which company produced the greatest percentage increase in the price per share over the year?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage increase on page 2.
The price per share at 1st Jan and 31st Dec for each company is needed for the calculations. The percentage increases in the price per share for each company are as follows:
Media: (290−250) ÷ 250 × 100 = 16%
Insurance: (380−350) ÷ 350 × 100 = 8.6%
Retail: (510−440) ÷ 440 × 100 = 15.9%
Energy: (355−300) ÷ 300 × 100 = 18.3%
Leisure: (230−190) ÷ 190 × 100 = 21.1%

Leisure produced the greatest percentage increase in the price per share over the year.

The answer is E (Leisure).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: In June, half of the shares in Insurance are sold at 402𝑝 per share. The money received is reinvested in the same company on 31st December. How many shares does the client hold in Insurance at the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
Half the number of shares: 6,500 ÷ 2 = 3,250.
Proceeds from half of the shares: 3,250 × 402𝑝 = 130,6500𝑝.
The number of shares bought on the 31st December: 130,6500𝑝 ÷ 380𝑝 = 3,438.2 ≈ 3,438.
The total number of Insurance shares (held all year + bought on the 31st Dec): 3,250 + 3,438 = 6,688.

The answer is B (6,688).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Between 1st January and 1st May the share price of Retail falls by 10%. What percentage increase in the price per share takes place between 1st May and 31st December?
questions.explanation:
A fall of 10% in the price per share means that on the 1st May shares are worth 90% of their value on the 1st January: 90% 𝑜𝑓 440𝑝 = 0.9 × 440𝑝 = 396𝑝.

If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage increase on page 2.
The price per share in Retail on the 1st May is 396𝑝.
The price per share in Retail on the 31st December is 510𝑝.
The percentage change between 1st May and 31st December in the price per share is:
(510−396) ÷ 396 × 100 = 28.78%.

The answer is A (28.78%).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Which of the following ratios best represents the ratio of the number of shares held in Retail and in Energy on 1st January?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition of ratio on page 2.
The number of shares held in Retail on the 1st January is 9,000.
The number of shares held in Energy on the 1st January is 13,500.
The ratio of the number of shares held in Retail and in Energy on the 1st January is:
9,000: 13,500 which simplified (both numbers divided by 4,500) is the same as 2: 3.

The answer is A (2: 3).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Over a 3 year period, the price per share of Leisure is expected to show the same annual percentage change as it does in the first year. What is the expected price per share of Leisure at the end of the 3 year period?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage change on page 2.
The price per share of Leisure on the 1st January is 190𝑝.
The price per share of Leisure on the 31st December is 230𝑝.
The percentage change between 1st January and 31st December is (230−190) ÷ 190 × 100 = 21%, which is also the annual percentage increase for the next two years.

The price per share increases each year and the next growth is calculated using the new price per share rather than the original value. There are two methods to finish answering this question:

Method 1
The price per share after 1 year (given in the question) is 230𝑝.
The price per share after 2 years: 230𝑝 + (21% 𝑜𝑓 230𝑝) = 230𝑝 + (0.21 × 230𝑝) = 278.179𝑝.
The price per share after 3 years: 278.179𝑝 + (21% 𝑜𝑓 278.179𝑝) = 278.179𝑝 + (0.21 × 278.179𝑝) = 336.59659𝑝 ≈ 337𝑝.

Method 2
This method is much faster as it involves a single calculation.
If needed, please refer to the formula on how to calculate the (compound) growth/decay on page 2 and make the necessary substitutions.
The new, increased price per share: 𝑁 = 𝑁0 × (multiplier)𝑛 = 190𝑝 × (1.21)3 = 336.6𝑝 ≈ 337𝑝 (by substituting 𝑁0 = 190𝑝, multiplier = 1.21, 𝑛 = 3).
The answer is C (337).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

sections.title: Team Profit
passages: This chart shows the annual profit made by two teams within a company over 5 years.

questions.prompt: Over the period Year 1 to Year 4 (inclusive) what is the total profit for Team 1?
questions.explanation:
The profit for Team 1 in Year 1 is £35,000.
The profit for Team 1 in Year 2 is £45,000.
The profit for Team 1 in Year 3 is £55,000.
The profit for Team 1 in Year 4 is £60,000.

The total profit for Team 1 for the period Year 1 to Year 4 is: £35,000 + £45,000 + £55,000 + £60,000 = £195,000.

The answer is D (£195,000).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: What is the greatest difference between the profits made by the two teams in a year?
questions.explanation:
The difference between Team 1 and Team 2 profits in Year 1 is: £45,000 − £35,000 = £10,000.
The difference between Team 1 and Team 2 profits in Year 2 is: £45,000 − £40,000 = £5,000.
The difference between Team 1 and Team 2 profits in Year 3 is: £55,000 − £40,000 = £15,000.
The difference between Team 1 and Team 2 profits in Year 4 is: £60,000 − £55,000 = £5,000.
The difference between Team 1 and Team 2 profits in Year 5 is: £50,000 − £45,000 = £5,000.

The greatest difference between the profits of Team 1 and Team 2 is £15,000 (in Year 3).

The answer is C (£15,000).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: What is the average annual profit for Team 2 over the 5 year period?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on how to calculate the average of numbers on page 2.
The sum of the profits for Team 2 over the five year period is: £45,000 + £40,000 + £40,000 + £55,000 + £50,000 = £230,000.
The average of the profits for Team 2 over the five year period is £230,000 ÷ 5 = £46,000.
The answer is A (£46,000).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Which of the following ratios best represents the ratio of profits between Team 1 in Year 2 and Team 2 in Year 4?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition of ratio on page 2.
The profit of Team 1 in Year 2 is £45,000.
The profit of Team 2 in Year 4 is £55,000.
The ratio of profits between Team 1 in Year 2 and Team 2 in Year 4 is 45,000: 55,000. This can be simplified to 9: 11 by dividing both numbers by 5,000.

The answer is E (9: 11).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: What is the percentage increase in total profits between Year 2 and Year 3?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage increase on page 2.
The total profit in Year 2 is £45,000 + £40,000 = £85,000.
The total profit in Year 3 is £55,000 + £40,000 = £95,000.
The percentage increase in total profits between Year 2 and Year 3 is (95,000−85,000) ÷ 85,000 × 100 = 11.8% (rounded to 1 d.p.).

The answer is A (11.8%).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Comparing each year, what is the smallest percentage contribution to annual profit made by Team 2?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on expressing one quantity as a percentage of another on page 2.
Profit for Team 2 for each year as well as total profit for each year are needed for calculations.
The percentage contributions made by Team 2 to the profit of that year are as follows:
Year 1: £45,000 ÷ (£35,000+£45,000) × 100 = 56.25%
Year 2: £40,000 ÷ (£45,000+£40,000) × 100 = 47.1%
Year 3: £40,000 ÷ (£55,000+£40,000) × 100 = 42.1%
Year 4: £55,000 ÷ (£60,000+£55,000) × 100 = 47.8%
Year 5: £50,000 ÷ (£45,000+£50,000) × 100 = 52.6%

The smallest percentage contribution made by Team 2 to the profit of that year is 42.1% in Year 3.

The answer is B (42.1%).

Note
Not all percentage contributions have to be calculated. By comparing the profits made by both teams for each year, one can see that in Year 2, 3, and 4, Team 2 contributed less than 50% (bar representing Team 2 is shorter than the one of Team 1). Moreover, in Year 3 the difference between the profits is the biggest. Therefore, only the percentage contribution made by Team 2 in Year 3 to the profit of that year could be calculated.
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: On the basis of the Year 5 profits a forecast is made for Year 6. It is predicted that Team 1 will increase their profits by 4% while Team 2’s profits will decrease by 4%. What will be the forecast for the percentage increase in total profits?
questions.explanation:
This is a two stage question.

The first stage is to calculate the total profit (sum of the profits of Team 1 and Team 2) in Year 6.
If needed, please refer to the formula on how to calculate the (compound) growth/decay on page 2 and make the following substitutions:
𝑁 is what needs to be found (total profit in Year 6 = sum of profits for Team 1 and 2 in Year 6).
𝑁0 are £45,000 for Team 1 in Year 5 and £50,000 for Team 2 in Year 5.
𝑚𝑢𝑙𝑡𝑖𝑝𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑠 are 1.04 for Team 1 in Year 5 (because of the 4% increase) and 0.96 for Team 2 in Year 5 (because of the 4% decrease).
𝑛 is 1 for both teams.
The total forecasted profit in Year 6 is: 𝑁 = £45,000 × (1.04)1 + £50,000 × (0.96)1 = £46,800 + £48,000 = £94,800

The second stage is to calculate the percentage increase in profits from Year 5 to Year 6.
If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage increase on page 2.
The total profit in Year 5 is £95,000.
The total (forecasted) profit in Year 6 is £94,800.
The percentage change in total profits between Year 5 and Year 6 is (94,800−95,000) ÷ 95,000 × 100 = −0.21% (rounded to 2 d.p.).

The answer is D (−0.21%).

sections.title: Employee Pay
passages: The table below shows the hours worked by five employees for a week. Any hours worked in excess of 35 are paid at ‘time and a half’.

questions.prompt: Which employee is paid the highest rate of pay per hour?
questions.explanation:
The question of finding the highest rate of pay per hour suggests the calculation that should be performed, i.e. pay should be divided by hours. Gross pay should be used as it is not affected by deductions.

Important information necessary in answering this question is: ‘any hours worked in excess of 35 are paid at “time and a half”’.

Firstly, for each person separately, any hours in excess of 35 need to be adjusted as they are paid at time and a half, and then the pay rate should be calculated:
Azhda
Hours = 23
Gross Pay = £300
Rate of pay = £300 ÷ 23 = £13.04 per hour

Bathusha
Hours = 35 + 2 × 1.5 = 35 + 3 = 38
Gross Pay = £400
Rate of pay = £400 ÷ 38 = £10.53 per hour

Chris
Hours = 35 + 5 × 1.5 = 35 + 7.5 = 42.5
Gross Pay = £500
Rate of pay = £500 ÷ 42.5 = £11.76 per hour

Dean
Hours = 35 + 7 × 1.5 = 35 + 10.5 = 45.5
Gross Pay = £520
Rate of pay = £520 ÷ 45.5 = £11.43 per hour

Emily
Hours = 33
Gross Pay = £380
Rate of pay = £380 ÷ 33 = £11.52 per hour

Azhda is paid the highest rate of pay per hour.

The answer is A (Azhda).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Which employee has the smallest percentage of deductions from gross pay?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on expressing one quantity as a percentage of another on page 2.
The values of Deductions and Gross Pay are needed for calculations. The percentage of deductions from gross pay for each employee are as follows:
Azhda: £70 ÷ £300 × 100 = 23.3%
Bathusha: £90 ÷ £400 × 100 = 22.5%
Chris: £110 ÷ £500 × 100 = 22.0%
Dean: £120 ÷ £520 × 100 = 23.1%
Emily: £80 ÷ £380 × 100 = 21.1%

Emily had the smallest percentage deduction from gross pay.

The answer is E (Emily).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: For how many of the employees is Net Pay less than 80% of their Gross Pay?
questions.explanation:
If needed, please refer to the formula on expressing one quantity as a percentage of another on page 2.
The percentage of Net Pay to the Gross Pay for each employee are as follows:
Azhda: £230 ÷ £300 × 100 = 76.7%
Bathusha: £310 ÷ £400 × 100 = 77.5%
Chris: £390 ÷ £500 × 100 = 78.0%
Dean: £400 ÷ £520 × 100 = 76.9%
Emily: £300 ÷ £380 × 100 = 78.9%

For all five employees Net Pay is less than 80% of their Gross Pay.

The answer is E (5).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: A backdated pay rise increases total gross pay by 1.5%. Total Deductions increase by 2%. By what percentage does Total Net Pay increase?
questions.explanation:
The total gross pay is £300 + £400 + £500 + £520 + £380 = £2,100.
The total deductions are £70 + £90 + £110 + £120 + £80 = £470.
The total net pay is £230 + £310 + £390 + £400 + £380 = £1,630.

If needed, please refer to the formula on how to calculate the (compound) growth/decay on page 2 and make the necessary substitutions.
The new, increased gross pay is 𝑁 = 𝑁0 × (multiplier)𝑛 = £2,100 × (1.015)1 = £2,131.5 (by substituting 𝑁0 = £2100, multiplier = 1.015, 𝑛 = 1).
The new, increased, deductions are 𝑁 = 𝑁0 × (multiplier)𝑛 = £470 × (1.02)1 = £479.4 (by substituting 𝑁0 = £470, multiplier = 1.02, 𝑛 = 1).
The new total Net Pay is £2,131.5 − £479.4 = £1,652.1.

If needed, please refer to the definition and formula on how to calculate the percentage change on page 2.
The old total Net Pay is £1,630.
The new total Net Pay is £1,652.1.
The percentage change in total net pays is (£1,652.1−£1,630) ÷ £1,630 × 100 = 1.36% (rounded to 2 d.p.).

The answer is C (1.36%).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key

questions.prompt: Consider the total of overtime hours worked by these employees. What percentage is worked by Grade I workers?
questions.explanation:
Azhda (Grade I worker) did not work any overtime.
Bathusha (Grade II worker) worked 37 − 35 = 2 hours of overtime.
Chris (Grade I worker) worked 40 − 35 = 5 hours of overtime.
Dean (Grade II worker) worked 42 − 35 = 7 hours of overtime.
Emily (Grade I worker) worked no overtime.

If needed, please refer to the formula on expressing one quantity as a percentage of another on page 2.
The total number of overtime hours worked is 2 + 5 + 7 = 14 and 5 of them were worked by a Grade I worker.
The percentage of overtime worked by Grade I workers to the total number of overtime hours is: 5 ÷ 14 × 100 = 35.71%.

The answer is B (35.71%).
questions.patternName: mathcentre / University of Hertfordshire · Official answer key
